sources.title: Quipu Administrative Records
sources.author: Inca Quipucamayoc
sources.excerpt: Knots in colored cords record tributes: 500 loads of potatoes, 200 llamas, 50 workers for road building.
sources.longExcerpt: The Inca Empire, largest in pre-Columbian America, ran without writing as Europeans knew it. Instead, quipucamayocs - keeper of the knots - recorded everything in quipu. Colored cords hang from a main string: red for war, yellow for gold, white for peace. Knots at different positions indicate numbers. This quipu records tribute from Cajamarca province: 500 loads of freeze-dried potatoes, 200 llamas, 50 workers for maintaining the royal road. An entire civilization's memory stored in textile.

sources.title: Inca Quipu Chronicles
sources.author: Inca quipucamayocs
sources.excerpt: The knotted cords record the tribute from each province, the number of warriors, and the harvests of each season. Each color and knot position tells its part of the great story of Tawantinsuyu.
sources.longExcerpt: The knotted cords record the tribute from each province, the number of warriors, and the harvests of each season. Each color and knot position tells its part of the great story of Tawantinsuyu. These quipu (khipu) recording devices were the sophisticated information storage system of the Inca Empire, using knotted strings to record numerical data, historical events, and possibly even narrative information.

sources.title: Guaraní Creation Songs
sources.author: Guaraní elders
sources.excerpt: In the beginning, Ñamandú created the earth through the power of sacred song. The first words brought forth the palm tree, the eternal fire, and the mist that carries the souls of our ancestors.
sources.longExcerpt: In the beginning, Ñamandú created the earth through the power of sacred song. The first words brought forth the palm tree, the eternal fire, and the mist that carries the souls of our ancestors. These creation myths of the Guaraní people of Paraguay and southern Brazil preserve ancient cosmological beliefs about the origins of the world and humanity.

sources.title: Mapuche War Chants
sources.author: Mapuche warriors
sources.excerpt: We are the people of the land, unconquered by the Inca, free in our forests and mountains. Our ancestors' spirits guide our spears, and the earth itself fights beside us.
sources.longExcerpt: We are the people of the land, unconquered by the Inca, free in our forests and mountains. Our ancestors' spirits guide our spears, and the earth itself fights beside us. The Mapuche people of Chile and Argentina maintained their independence against Inca expansion and later Spanish colonization, preserving their traditions through oral poetry and ceremonial chants.

citation.modernSource: Anales de la Universidad de Chile, 1897
